questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a goal of forensic incident response?

options.text: Wiping the affected systems immediately, before anything is examined
options.rationale: Correct choice: that destroys the evidence.

options.text: Learning what happened
Learning how far the attack spread
Preserving the evidence

questions.explanation: Forensic incident response uses forensic techniques to learn what happened, how far it spread, and why, while preserving evidence. It isn't only about restoring service.

questions.stem: What does attack attribution identify, compared with identifying the technique an attacker used?

options.text: The actor behind the attack, not just the method, and only with some uncertainty
Only the malware family
options.rationale: That is closer to identifying the technique or tool.

options.text: Only the vulnerability that was exploited
options.rationale: That is the weakness, not the actor.

options.text: Only the victim

questions.explanation: Attack attribution identifies who is behind an attack from evidence such as TTPs, infrastructure, malware, and timing. It is uncertain, because evidence can be spoofed or planted.
questions.discriminator_tested: Attribution identifies the actor, with uncertainty.

questions.stem: An attacker emails a booby-trapped document to an employee, who opens it, and it exploits a flaw in the document reader. In the Cyber Kill Chain, which stage is the email itself?

options.text: Delivery
options.rationale: Correct: getting the weapon to the target.

options.text: Weaponization
options.rationale: Weaponization is building the malicious document, before it is sent.

options.text: Exploitation
options.rationale: Exploitation is the flaw being triggered when the file is opened.

options.text: Installation
options.rationale: Installation is persistent malware being placed on the system.

questions.explanation: The Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain stages are reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, and actions on objectives. Sending the weapon to the target is delivery.
questions.discriminator_tested: Delivery = getting the weapon to the target.

questions.stem: Which statement about the MITRE ATT&CK matrix is NOT true?

options.text: It is a seven-step linear sequence that every attack must follow
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: that describes the Cyber Kill Chain.

options.text: It is a knowledge base of real-world adversary behavior
Tactics form the columns, with techniques beneath them
It is used to map detection coverage

questions.explanation: The MITRE ATT&CK matrix is a knowledge base of real-world adversary tactics and techniques. It is not linear: tactics (why) are the columns and techniques (how) sit beneath them.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the four features of the Diamond Model?

options.text: Exploitation
options.rationale: Correct choice: exploitation is a Kill Chain stage.

options.text: Adversary
Infrastructure
Victim

questions.explanation: The Diamond Model describes an intrusion event through four features: adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim.
questions.discriminator_tested: Diamond features: adversary, capability, infrastructure, victim.

questions.stem: Why are TTPs more valuable to defend against than IoCs such as IP addresses or file hashes?

options.text: They describe behavior, which is much harder for attackers to change than an IP address or a hash
options.rationale: Correct: attackers can swap an IP or recompile malware easily, but changing how they operate is costly.

options.text: Each TTP is unique to a single attack
options.rationale: TTPs recur across a group's attacks, which is what makes them useful.

options.text: IoCs never change
TTPs are legally required

questions.explanation: TTPs are tactics, techniques, and procedures that describe attacker behavior. They are behavior-based and harder for attackers to change than IoCs such as IPs or hashes.
questions.discriminator_tested: TTPs are harder for attackers to change than IoCs.

questions.stem: Which two are artifacts and sources of evidence in a digital investigation? (Choose two.)

options.text: A memory capture from the affected server
Firewall and system logs
A vendor's marketing brochure
The company's organization-chart poster
A sealed, never-used USB stick from the supply cupboard
options.rationale: It has never touched the incident.

questions.explanation: Artifacts and sources of evidence include logs, memory, disk images, network captures, registry data, browser history, email, device and cloud data, and metadata. Volatile data is collected first.
questions.discriminator_tested: Evidence sources include memory, logs, images, and captures.

questions.stem: Which practice is NOT part of proper evidence handling?

options.text: Letting anyone browse the evidence locker without logging it
options.rationale: Correct choice: access to evidence must be controlled and documented.

options.text: Labeling each item
Storing evidence securely
Documenting every transfer

questions.explanation: Evidence handling means collecting, labeling, storing, transferring, and controlling access to evidence, with documentation at every step.
questions.discriminator_tested: Evidence handling controls and documents access.

questions.stem: Which two practices help with preserving digital evidence? (Choose two.)

options.text: Using a write blocker when imaging the drive
options.rationale: Correct: nothing can be written to the original.

options.text: Comparing the hashes of the original and the copy
options.rationale: Correct: matching hashes show the copy is unchanged.

options.text: Examining the original drive directly
options.rationale: Work from the copy, never the original.

options.text: Defragmenting the drive before imaging it
options.rationale: That rewrites data on the original.

options.text: Booting the suspect's PC to look around
options.rationale: Booting changes data on the drive.

questions.explanation: Preserving digital evidence means making bit-for-bit forensic copies, working from the copy, using write blockers, and verifying integrity with hashes. Never examine the original.
questions.discriminator_tested: Write blockers and hash verification preserve evidence.

questions.stem: Which statement about chain of custody is NOT true?

options.text: A missing entry doesn't matter as long as the evidence looks fine
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: any gap undermines integrity and admissibility.

options.text: It records who handled the evidence
It records when, where, and why
A gap can make evidence inadmissible

questions.explanation: Chain of custody is the documented record of who handled evidence, when, where, and why. A gap undermines integrity and admissibility.
